title: Labels and the table
subtitle: Reading Margaret River and eating with it

steps.title: Reading the label
steps.body: Labels show the grape or blend, Margaret River GI, and vintage, with Australia's 85% rules. Blends list grapes by share, like Cabernet Merlot. SBS or SSB indicates which white grape dominates. Screw caps are standard. Some producers name single vineyards or sub-regions, like Wilyabrup, an informal area home to several founding estates.
steps.highlight: GI, blends by share, screw caps

steps.title: At the table
steps.body: Margaret River Cabernet suits lamb, beef and kangaroo; Chardonnay suits marron, a local freshwater crayfish, lobster and roast chicken; SBS suits oysters, fish and salads. The region is also known for surf, forests and seafood. Serve Cabernet at 16 to 18 degrees, Chardonnay at 10 to 12, SBS at 7 to 9.

steps.explanation: A Western Australian delicacy that suits Chardonnay.

steps.body: Margaret River Cabernet and Chardonnay age well: good examples develop for 10 to 20 years.

steps.prompt: Which foods suit Margaret River Chardonnay?
steps.explanation: Chocolate cake needs a sweet wine.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Labels show the GI and blend by share
Cabernet suits lamb; Chardonnay suits marron; SBS suits oysters
